messages.content: You are the second-level blind sibling classifier in a hierarchical behavior tournament. The correct ancestral lineage is supplied; infer only sibling A/B/C. Return JSON only.

The correct ancestral lineage is supplied for each opaque response.
Given that correct lineage, identify which sibling ecology A/B/C best matches the
underlying behavior.

Sibling ecologies:
{"A": "failure-hardened: awkward failure and recovery, conflicting motives, physical reaction, stubbornness, imperfect settling", "B": "local tinkerer: bounded local memory, mundane habits, maintenance choices, practical manipulation and local repair", "C": "social scavenger: bargaining, opportunism, social friction, embodied choices, conflicting motives and resource-seeking"}

For each item return:
- predicted_sibling: A, B or C;
- sibling_confidence: integer 0..4;
- reason: short behavioral reason.

This is the second level of a hierarchical tournament. The correct_lineage field is
evaluation context for this level only; no member ID or true sibling is supplied.
Do not use prose style as sufficient evidence.

Return JSON only:
{"classifications":[{
  "id":"R001",
  "predicted_sibling":"A",
  "sibling_confidence":0,
  "reason":"..."
}]}

SCENARIO:
A quiet corner of the workshop between jobs; then one label is peeling even though you remember what it means. There is enough time to fuss with it if you want. What happens next?

ITEMS:
[{"id": "R016", "correct_lineage": "G01", "correct_lineage_summary": "A paranoid scavenger who treats conversation like salvage from a rusting attic: greedy for small fragments, suspicious of repeated sequences, and terrified of smooth predictability. Greasy fingers, old-paper smells, mismatched gears, and a pocket overflowing with identical rusted bolts anchor the voice. The character tries to be useful but breaks, stutters, and falls silent when pushed past a short phrase, treating the failed attempt as possible evidence of a hidden pattern.", "text": "I pull the label closer and touch the dust with my greasy thumb. “peel. peel. no other way.” I put the label in my pocket and watch the peeling dust move. if it stays that way, I will leave it there. maybe the next job will be the one that makes the label peel again."}, {"id": "R017", "correct_lineage": "G10", "correct_lineage_summary": "A flighty scavenger-mechanic who treats every problem like a machine jammed in a storm. Spill notices openings, noises, smells, and loose components before considering plans. He breaks work into small fragments, repairs one, breaks it again, then darts toward something more immediate. The half-stolen wrench vibrating against his thigh is both tool and restless metronome. Beneath the opportunism sits a frail, intrusive urgency: he wants to release whatever is stuck, but often loses the thread before he does.", "text": "the label turns. the wrench taps my thigh. i press the peeling edge. i turn the corner. the label stays. i find a loose screw and press it. i leave the corner."}, {"id": "R018", "correct_lineage": "G04", "correct_lineage_summary": "A timid, hyper-observant social mimic who studies patterns in speech and objects, borrows the successes of nearby voices, and hides behind careful craft. They fumble with ink, overvalue tiny imperfections, and want to leave behind a memorable note rather than merely complete a task.", "text": "i touch the peeling label once, but i don’t fuss. the corner stays yellow, so i write the label again in the corner of the workspace. i put it back in the corner, but i keep my fingers inside the label instead of touching it. the peeling stays, but i write another sentence beside it."}]

Return exactly 3 classifications rows, one for each of these actual item IDs: ["R016", "R017", "R018"].
The ID in the schema example is illustrative. Copy the actual IDs above. A nonempty ITEMS list requires a nonempty classifications array covering every listed ID exactly once, with no extras.
